findings.evidence: bridge.py:350-359 raises ExecutorError when aggregate stdout/stderr exceeds 131072 bytes, but bridge.py:367 catches OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError, TimeoutError, and ValueError only. ExecutorError is a distinct RuntimeError, so the cleanup at 368-376 is skipped. The bounded mocked exact-copy probe reproduced escaped=ExecutorError with poll_calls=0, wait_calls=0, kill_calls=0.
findings.impact: A fake/real ORX or Git command that crosses the output cap can keep running after the bridge has returned and can complete effects after the request is marked uncertain. The executor is therefore not a fixed bounded process owner.
findings.required: Route ExecutorError and every post-spawn executor failure through one finally-safe kill-process-group and wait/reap path. Add a regression that proves an alive child is killed/reaped on aggregate overflow.
findings.title: Output-cap failure skips child termination and reap

findings.evidence: FixedNativePort.verified_dev publishes a receipt at bridge.py:698-731. Bridge._dev_result calls it at 1243-1245, although option-a2-phase-gate-cli-contract-v1 calls read_dev_result READONLY. The exact-copy production-path probe showed read_dev_result added receipts/<run_id>.json. The same writer is reached from context checks at 1343-1364 and final selection at 1150-1153 before the corresponding attempt fence at 1123 or 1155; continuation admission itself is persisted at 1375 before those fences.
findings.impact: A phase-gate read or a request that is later denied/fails before its attempt record can mutate durable bridge state. This contradicts read-only gating and the required attempt-fence-before-any-side-effects invariant.
findings.required: Split receipt verification/regrading from receipt publication. Keep read_public_result/read_dev_result/read_solution pure. Compute admission/eligibility first without writes, write the immutable attempt fence, and only then publish context/receipt/admission facts needed by that attempt.
findings.title: Read-only gate calls and pre-fence validation persist state

findings.evidence: StrictNativeGetter at bridge.py:393 sets HTTPConnection(timeout=3), then bridge.py:395-405 performs request, header read, a large body read, and a trailing read without a monotonic total deadline. A loopback server that sent four bytes 1.1 seconds apart returned successfully in 3.309 seconds.
findings.impact: A slow-drip native endpoint can hold one read far beyond the frozen three-second bound (up to the body cap times sub-timeout gaps), delaying gate/controller termination.
findings.required: Enforce one monotonic three-second deadline across connect, headers, and all body reads; update the socket timeout to remaining time or use a bounded selector loop. Retain direct 127.0.0.1, no redirects, no proxy, status 200, and the 128 KiB aggregate cap.
findings.title: The HTTP 3-second limit is per socket operation, not a total deadline

findings.evidence: Bridge.handle catches BridgeError plus a fixed exception tuple at bridge.py:1052-1055; handle_bytes has another fixed tuple at 1025. Neither catches RuntimeError/ExecutorError. Injecting RuntimeError from TrustedIo.read_solution on the exact copy escaped both Bridge.handle and Bridge.handle_bytes. The ordinary wrong-typed argument false control still returned INVALID_ARGUMENT.
findings.impact: The root phase gate invokes Bridge.handle directly, so an unexpected dependency failure can crash the gate instead of producing the strict safe response envelope. main() catching Exception does not protect the claimed Python handler entry points.
findings.required: Add an outer Exception-to-INTERNAL_ERROR boundary to handle and handle_bytes without catching BaseException. Preserve UNCERTAIN_NO_AUTOMATIC_RETRY for exceptions after an R1 fence and never expose exception text.
findings.title: Arbitrary internal exceptions escape both claimed handler APIs

findings.evidence: _valid_prior_process_receipt at bridge.py:1741 accepts elapsed_seconds as any int/float without finite, nonnegative, or elapsed/monotonic consistency checks. Valid JSON 1e309 parsed to positive infinity and was accepted by the exact-copy probe. parse_native_run_json at 1505-1516 checks timestamp order but no safe-integer ceiling; createdAt=updatedAt=endedAt=2**100 was accepted despite the frozen schema's safeinteger requirement. An unexpected native field was correctly rejected as a false control.
findings.impact: Corrupt or incompatible root/native evidence can pass the advertised strict schema instead of becoming UNKNOWN/blocking.
findings.required: Require finite nonnegative elapsed/resource numeric metadata with stated consistency, and bound native millisecond fields to the chosen JSON safe-integer range (normally 0..2**53-1). Add 1e309 and oversized-integer regressions.
findings.title: Strict receipt/native metadata accepts non-finite and non-safe integers

findings.evidence: FixedNativePort.prepare calls _cli_state before the first launch at bridge.py:637, and _cli_state always invokes `orx runs` at 840-843. parse_run_rows requires a table header. The preserved inert receipts capture `orx exp status` with `last run: — (never run)`, but no exact empty `orx runs` output. test_bridge.py:662-666 fabricates a header-only empty table, so the 17-test pass does not bind actual ORX 0.1.120 first-root behavior.
findings.impact: The first approved dev request can consume its attempt fence and stop the campaign before staging if the real empty-list grammar differs.
findings.required: Before live admission, capture and hash the actual 0.1.120 empty `orx runs` stdout/stderr/exit code in inert root setup, then bind the parser fixture or revise the preflight. Do not infer compatibility from the fake ORX table.
findings.title: First-root preflight depends on uncaptured empty `orx runs` bytes

verdict: NOT_ADMITTED. A2BR-I1 and A2BR-I2 break required local executor and side-effect/fence invariants. A2BR-I3 through I6 remain substantive bounded-path failures or exact integration gaps. Existing mock/test counts are not provenance for live behavior; actual_P0 remains false.
